unmapped_findings: For Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al, aging for 24 h increases YS, UTS, and hardness to levels twice as high as in the as-homogenized state and drastically reduces ductility (opposite trend to the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy).

The specific total elongation (TE) for the 550 °C/24 h condition at 8 wt.% Al is not separately reported in Fig. 3c; at 8Al, TE falls to near 10% for the sibling 500 °C/24 h and 600 °C/24 h conditions.

The strengthening is attributed to formation of nm-sized κ-carbides during aging; the paper additionally states (in the context of Fig. 5, aged at 600 °C) that these κ-carbides are thermally very stable at 600 °C and prevail after 100 h with only modest coarsening.
